pr.title: Add and update contacts from the command line
pr.head: 46934ce08f929da04765fbc327ec3eb76aaf0f93

summary: This adds msg contacts add and msg contacts update. Both run in msgd, which drives Contacts.app over Apple Events, so the Automation grant for Contacts belongs to the daemon rather than the terminal. That is the same model sending already uses (contact-writing.md §2).

Apple Events won over CNContactStore because the note field needs a restricted entitlement that a self-signed bundle cannot carry (§3). The logic that decides what to write sits in tested Rust above a ContactStore trait, and single-purpose AppleScripts for find, create, values, append, and set sit below it. Tests inject a fake store, so cargo test writes to nobody's contacts (§6).
The wire protocol moves from 18 to 19 for the new person-add and person-update commands.

cards.title: Write semantics
cards.html:
FlagBehaviour
--phone, --emailAppended, skipped when handle_key already matches
--title, --org, --noteReplaced outright; an empty value clears the field
--duplicate (add)Adds a second person with a name Contacts already holds

Exit status: 0 wrote, 1 failure, 2 grant missing, 3 ambiguous term.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• Round 1 at a48b260 opened five P2 findings. Rounds at 53da4d6 and 13bcfc8 fixed all five and opened one more, about two comments that still described the old name match.
  • 46934ce rewrites those two comments, so all six finding threads are fixed and resolved, and the review at this head is clean.
  • The review's suggestions, none blocking: the FIND pairing loop is quadratic in the number of cards (about 6s at 10,000 cards and 24s at 20,000 on synthetic lists, against the CLI's 30s deadline), and it pairs four separately fetched lists by position.

groups.title: The wire contract
groups.kicker: Two new commands, a reply shape, and protocol 19
intro: PersonAddRequest and PersonUpdateRequest carry field values and no filesystem paths, so the protocol's §6 rule is unaffected. PersonWriteReply returns the printable changed and unchanged lines, which the CLI prints as they are and --json passes through.
concepts: An older daemon fails at the version gate, so the error it shows tells the user to reinstall it.

checks.text: COMMANDS lists both new names, and the round-trip test covers both variants.

files.note: New request and reply types, plus the protocol 19 note

groups.title: The write core and the osascript boundary
groups.kicker: Duplicate guard, resolve-then-apply, dedup, and the scripts
intro: add collapses whitespace in the name, requires at least one phone or email, and rejects empty values before any Apple Event runs. It then refuses a name that find already answers to unless --duplicate is set, and creates the card. update resolves its term through the index exactly as resolve does, finds the cards filed under that name, writes to the first, and counts values on every one of those cards as already present (§7).

apply reads the card's existing phones and emails, keys them with handle_key, appends only values it has not seen, and sets text fields. Scripts receive their arguments through on run rather than string interpolation.
concepts: Error -1743 from a refused Apple Event maps to AccessDenied, which is exit 2.

checks.text: FIND fetches each person's id, first name, last name, and organization. filed_as matches them with filed_name, the resolver's rule, ignoring case and extra whitespace, so the display order never affects the match.
Fields::check runs before find or create in both add and update.
The comments in update and on update_addresses_the_card_by_its_filed_name describe matching by filed_name, not by Contacts.app's name.

files.note: The whole feature: trait, scripts, add, update, apply, and unit tests against a fake
filed_name is extracted here so the resolver and the writer share one naming rule

groups.title: Daemon wiring
groups.kicker: Injecting the store, serializing writes, and dropping the cache
intro: DaemonOptions gains contacts_store, which defaults to ContactsApp. Each add or update holds the contact_writes mutex from start to finish, so two connections cannot both pass the duplicate guard. The cached index is dropped after every write, whether it succeeded or not.

checks.text: Code takes contact_writes before contacts, never the other way round.

groups.title: CLI and client
groups.kicker: The new subcommands and the refusal without a daemon
intro: msg contacts add|update build the requests. Source refuses both unless it is talking to the daemon, and --no-names refuses every contacts subcommand.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The daemon harness with a fake store, and the CLI refusals
intro: The daemon harness injects FakeContacts, and so does every other daemon a test builds, including the permission-denied test and the concurrency test's SlowContacts. The CLI tests set MSG_DB, which forces the direct path, where both commands refuse before reaching any daemon.

checks.text: Every DaemonOptions in tests/daemon.rs sets contacts_store to a fake.
